remeasure.why: Any change to the measured module's blob invalidates these rows: the gate would then be comparing shipped F005 against a rule nobody has swept.
remeasure.command: uv run --package runcoach-api python .shipyard/spec/references/T130-overlap-sweep-harness.py t162-gate --f005 <shipped F005 module, `git show 42f7705:runcoach-api/src/runcoach_api/metrics/hrv_trend.py`> --rows .shipyard/spec/references/T162-no-regression-rows.csv --rowdir .shipyard/research/T239-rowdir --procs <n>
remeasure.runtime: ~13 minutes at --procs 16 on an otherwise idle machine (1,353,000 judgings)
remeasure.then: re-commit the regenerated runcoach-api/tests/data/T162-no-regression-rows.csv (only if its bytes actually moved), the mirrored spec/references/F006-no-regression-report.md, and this file with the new measured_module.blob_sha, its introducing commit and today's date. The command carries --rowdir .shipyard/research/T239-rowdir (<data>/research/T239-rowdir), so one run produces both the rows and the per-row CSVs test_hrv25_population.py counts; after that run, and only after it, rewrite that rowdir's measured-module.json with the blob_sha of the module the run measured: the test reds when its sidecar names another blob than this file does (sprint-009 review S7). The sidecar is tamper-evident only (review S11): it binds nothing unless the re-measurer writes it after a real --rowdir run, and the test's red does not print the blob to paste. A run that reproduces the rows byte for byte still has to happen and still has to be recorded: the identical bytes are the finding.
